text: On 19 July 2023, Harcourts real estate agent Yanfei Bao went missing in Christchurch's Wigram suburb after being last seen in Hornby, where she was scheduled to show a potential buyer a property on Trevor Street. She had a four-minute conversation with her friend Jin Tian during the morning, in which she inquired about transferring NZ$600,000 from China to pay for a house. Bao was reported missing after failing to collect her daughter from after-school care later that day. Her car was found in Wigram that evening, and her cellphone was discovered two days later on the Christchurch Southern Motorway. On 24 July 2023, 52-year-old Tingjun Cao was charged with kidnapping Bao after attempting to flee to China on 22 July 2023 and was arrested at Christchurch Airport. Cao, who claimed he had lost his job a month earlier and had poor eyesight, told police he did not "really" know Bao and had been traveling in his car looking for work. On 26 July 2023, the New Zealand Police launched a homicide investigation into Bao's disappearance. By 31 July 2023, search efforts were temporarily suspended due to high water levels in the Halswell River and Lake Ellesmere / Te Waihora, and police had received over 200 pieces of information, searching three properties under "Operation Helo." They were also seeking a silver Mitsubishi sedan, specifically registration DPH101, and a roughly 1 metre long flat-bottomed spade. On 7 August 2023, the search shifted to roads and farmland near Greenpark, and on 8 August, police confirmed recovering more items of interest. On 6 September 2023, searches expanded to include Christchurch and Rolleston. In October, police continued focusing on the Halswell River and Greenpark area and asked the public for sightings of clothing and a spade. On 19 January 2024, Detective Inspector Nicola Reeves reiterated the search was ongoing, specifically for a silver Mitsubishi 380 with registration DPH101. By July 2024, the investigation team had been reduced to eight investigators, and Reeves confirmed renewed search activity in previously searched and newly identified areas, including Greenpark, where a prior search had failed to yield results. On 30 July 2024, police found Bao's remains in a shallow grave, 15cm deep, along the treeline at a rural property in Greenpark, Lincoln, with over 60 officers involved in a 90-minute search. A post-mortem on 31 July 2024 confirmed the remains were Bao's, and on 2 August 2024, Reeves stated the news brought closure to the investigation and that Bao would be returned to her family. On 15 August 2023, Cao was formally charged with a single murder and pleaded not guilty, with police seeking information about a tracksuit, top, and spade. On 1 September 2023, Cao was officially identified as the suspect, and his lawyer withdrew interim name suppression. He appeared via audio-visual link at the Christchurch High Court, was remanded in custody, and continued to appear in court until December 2023. A tentative trial date of 24 October 2024 was set, and the trial began early on 21 October 2024 with a six-week duration presided over by Justice Lisa Preston, featuring a jury of six men and six women. The Crown was represented by prosecutors Cameron Stuart and Pip Currie, and the defence initially by Colin Eason and Joshua Macleod, though Cao later represented himself and appointed Eason and Macleod as standby counsel. The Crown presented evidence including CCTV footage, phone polling, geolocation data, and a six-hour police interview of Cao, as well as testimony from witnesses such as Detective Constable Andrew Calder, Bao's partner Paul Gooch, builder Mervin Boclot, colleagues, friends, and relatives, hardware store owner Dennis Shrimpton, and Cao's former employer Chun-Chieh (Jason) Li. The Crown also submitted footage of Bao purchasing a spade at a hardware store in New Brighton on the day of her murder. Police were able to track Bao's cellphone movements around Halswell Village and Tai Tapu cell tower, and forensic analysis of Bao's phone messages was conducted by Joshua Locke. During the trial, Cao testified on 29 November, claiming he had gone to Trevor Street but that Bao was not inside, and that he met a stranger named Mr Tang who tested his car and used his phone. Cao claimed Mr Tang communicated with him via walkie talkie and that DNA on his shoes belonged to multiple people, but prosecutor Pip Currie challenged this as "completely fictitious," citing Cao's earlier admission that he was the only one using the car during the disappearance and that he had owned the phone. On 3 December, Currie delivered the Crown's closing address, arguing that Cao had lured Bao to the property under false pretenses, attacked her, transported her to MacArtneys Road, murdered her, bought a spade, and buried her in a shallow grave in Greenpark. On the same day, the jury found Cao guilty after a one and a half hour deliberation. Bao's partner Paul Gooch welcomed the verdict, criticized Cao's lack of remorse, and thanked the police and his stepdaughter's school. Detective Inspector Nicola Reeves also welcomed the resolution and expressed empathy for Bao's family. Cao was remanded in custody for sentencing, scheduled for 7 March 2025. On 13 June 2025, at the Christchurch High Court, Cao was sentenced to life imprisonment with a minimum non-parole term of 17 years and five months by Justice Lisa Preston, who criticized Cao for sexually assaulting Bao and for lacking remorse. The Crown had sought a maximum sentence of 18 years due to the "brutal" nature of the crime and Cao's "callous" conduct, while defence lawyer Colin Eason argued for a minimum of 17 years, citing Cao's isolation due to language barriers and separation from family. Cao maintained his innocence, alleging a fictional Mr Tang had murdered Bao. Victim impact statements were delivered by Bao's 11-year-old daughter, husband Paul Gooch, father-in-law David Gooch, and her 74-year-old father (via video link from China). Detective Inspector Nicola Reeves paid tribute to Bao and her family. A Givealittle fundraising page, established by Bao's friend Vani Liu, raised over NZ$50,000 by August 2023 to support her family and relatives in China. On 18 November 2024, a public memorial service for Yanfei Bao was held at Our Lady of Victories Church in Sockburn, with Paul Gooch, her father, and sister delivering eulogies.
